2609.24895.title: Human-LLM Deliberation as Interactive Proof: Conditions for Verifiability Without Transparency
2609.24895.paper_summary: When an LLM supplies an argument that a user could not readily construct, how can the user decide whether to accept its claim? Inspired by interactive proofs, we model human-LLM deliberation as an interaction between a prover with unrestricted internal search and a resource-bounded human verifier. The verifier requests and checks supporting details without access to the LLM's internal state. Passed checks accumulate evidence toward an acceptance threshold. We prove anytime-valid soundness against adaptive provers: the probability of ever accepting a false claim is at most a chosen error level, provided the task supplies bounds on false passes and human checking errors that remain valid after every relevant history. A finite-horizon completeness bound additionally requires bounds on the adequacy of honest responses and sufficient diagnostic progress. Further checks can strengthen the evidence for acceptance, but each requires another adequate response and reliable human effort. Whether this tradeoff permits certification depends on the verifier's effort budget, cognitive load, expertise, and fatigue. We identify conditions under which the supplied bounds certify a specified sequence of local checks but not a specified global check under the same resource budgets.
2609.24895.paper_summary_zh: 當一個大型語言模型（LLM）提供一個用戶無法輕易構建的論點時，用戶如何決定是否接受其主張？受到互動證明的啟發，我們將人類與LLM的審議建模為一個具有不受限制內部搜索的證明者與一個資源受限的人類驗證者之間的互動。驗證者在沒有訪問LLM內部狀態的情況下請求並檢查支持細節。通過的檢查會累積證據，直至達到接受閾值。我們證明了對自適應證明者的隨時有效的健全性：接受虛假主張的概率至多為選定的錯誤水平，前提是任務提供了對虛假通過和人類檢查錯誤的界限，這些界限在每個相關歷史之後仍然有效。有限範圍的完整性界限還要求對誠實回應的充分性和足夠的診斷進展有界限。進一步的檢查可以加強接受的證據，但每次都需要另一個充分的回應和可靠的人類努力。這種權衡是否允許認證取決於驗證者的努力預算、認知負荷、專業知識和疲勞。我們確定了在提供的界限下，證明特定的局部檢查序列但不證明在相同資源預算下的特定全局檢查的條件。
